account:
It is just after seven on day 1. I have read today's updated appointments and the secretary's inquiry report. My day includes office business at eight, a grain inspection at the mill at ten, lunch at home, council letters at thirteen, tea with the neighbour at fifteen, office at sixteen-thirty, and a great hall lighting inspection at eighteen before returning home at nineteen.

The unusual confirmed development is the builder's installation of eight lanterns in the great hall. The builder asked me to inspect them and give my opinion, explicitly saying no accounts or approvals were needed. The secretary recorded the appointment with my agreement. The builder is now beside the town hall carrying a lantern. I know the lighting is intended to make the hall better lit, but I do not know whether it serves any special occasion.

There has also been unreliable chatter about lights or decorations at the bakery and a bridge or port change. The neighbour identified Townsfolk 02 as the source, could not establish what they actually witnessed, and said the baker knew of no celebration. I have not seen those decorations myself, so I cannot connect that chatter to the hall lighting or conclude that a celebration is planned.

The town account figures remain unresolved. At my request the secretary searched the four great hall table chests: three were empty and one contained bread, with no records identifying who holds the figures. No figures or council letters had reached the secretary when that report was written. The bread is worth noticing, but I do not know why it was there. For now I should thank the secretary, ask about any fresh business, and keep today's appointments rather than treat rumours as facts.
